source_read: Publisher HTML (Springer Nature Link, Harm Reduct J 21:14, open access), read in full in the built-in browser: all text sections, Funding and Competing interests; Table 1 on its own page (/tables/1); Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 read cell by cell on the full-size images (/figures/1, /figures/2). Supplementary files (Additional files 1-3, TIFF/DOCX downloads, including Fig. S2 urine data) not opened.

claims.note: Halifax part checked against text and Fig. 1: 11 of the 13 analogues positive on all five lots (carfentanil among them), sufentanil on the two 2017 lots only, alfentanil and U-47700 never. Two details the claim could add: the 2017 lots detected sufentanil only at 10 000 ng/mL and above, and two 2021 lots (188, 196) detected carfentanil only at 10 000 ng/mL and above. 'At up to 10 µg/mL' matches the Methods, but Fig. 1 has a 50 000 ng/mL row (negative for alfentanil and U-47700 there too), so the claim is conservative. For the 2021 lots several analogues (acetyl fentanyl, beta-hydroxythiofentanyl, THF fentanyl, p-fluorofentanyl) read positive at or below those lots' fentanyl limit (200 ng/mL), so 'well above those at which they detect fentanyl' holds for the 2017 lots more than for the 2021 lots. The panel was the authors' '13 most cited' analogues, consistent with the claim's caveat that panels were not chosen by market frequency. Minor: the authors' ten- to fiftyfold gain for the four analogues the 2021 lots detected better is 5-fold for acetyl fentanyl on lots 018 and 188 (500 against 100 ng/mL) by Fig. 1.

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Fig. 1
anchors.extracted: All five BTNX Rapid Response (20 ng/mL) lots cross-reacted with 11 fentanyl analogues: 3-methylfentanyl, acetyl fentanyl, acrylfentanyl, beta-hydroxythiofentanyl, butyrylfentanyl, carfentanil, cyclopropylfentanyl, fluorobutyrylfentanyl, furanyl fentanyl, p-fluorofentanyl, tetrahydrofuran fentanyl. The two 2017 lots (082, 004) also detected sufentanil (Fig. 1: only at 10 000 and 50 000 ng/mL); the three 2021 lots did not. No lot detected alfentanil or the non-fentanyl opioid U-47700 at any concentration (Fig. 1: negative in every cell up to 50 000 ng/mL).

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 1 (cells)
anchors.extracted: Limits differed by lot and analogue. Lowest positive concentration (ng/mL), lots 004/082 (2017) and 018/188/196 (2021): fentanyl 20/20/200/200/200; 3-methylfentanyl 500/500/1000/1000/500; acetyl fentanyl 500/500/100/100/50; acrylfentanyl 100/100/500/500/100; beta-OH-thiofentanyl 1000/1000/100/100/100; butyrylfentanyl 100/100/200/500/200; carfentanil 500/500/1000/10 000/10 000; cyclopropylfentanyl 100/100/200/500/100; fluorobutyrylfentanyl 5000 on all; furanyl fentanyl 5000/5000/500/500/200; p-fluorofentanyl 5000/5000/200/200/100; THF fentanyl 100 on all; sufentanil 10 000 (2017 lots only). Authors: 2021 lots 10 to 50 times more sensitive for four analogues, less sensitive for acrylfentanyl (except lot 196), butyrylfentanyl and carfentanil.

anchors.locator: Methods › Strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 6th paragraph
anchors.extracted: Pure analytical standards spiked into water at 10 ng/mL to 10 µg/mL, each lot in duplicate, read within 5 min by two people and recorded by consensus (no individual readings, no kappa). Panel = the 13 'most cited' fentanyl analogues plus U-47700; many other analogues untested; visual reading called subjective.

anchors.locator: Fig. 1 against Methods › Strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Fig. 1 shows a 50 000 ng/mL row not in the Methods list (top 10 µg/mL). Two non-monotone series: carfentanil lot 018 positive at 50 000, 10 000 and 1000 but negative at 5000 and 500 ng/mL; acrylfentanyl lot 196 positive at 100 but negative at 200 ng/mL. Fig. 1 gives one consensus cell per lot and concentration, so how the duplicate strips were combined is not shown.

claims.overstatement: The diphenhydramine part of 'false positives ... at concentrations 10 to 200 times lower' is not shown by the source: the 2017 lots were tested with diphenhydramine only at 150, 100 and 50 mg/mL (Fig. 2, other cells 'Not tested'), and at 50 mg/mL the 2021 lots also read negative, so a 2017 negative at 50 mg/mL does not mean the 2017 lots would not react at 0.5-25 mg/mL. At 100 mg/mL the 2017 lots were positive while 2021 lots 188 and 196 were negative. The contrast is shown directly only for lidocaine (2021 lots positive at 25 and 50 mg/mL, where 2017 lots were negative; 40-fold) and MDMA (2021 positive at 25 mg/mL, 2017 negative; 10 to 20-fold); suggested wording: 'with lidocaine and MDMA at concentrations 10 to 40 times lower, and with diphenhydramine from 0.5-1 mg/mL, a range the 2017 lots were not tested in'.
claims.note: All numbers match the text and Figs. 1-2: fentanyl in water 20 ng/mL (2017 lots) against 200 ng/mL (2021 lots), ten times higher (200/20 = 10); in urine 50 ng/mL (018, 196) and 100 ng/mL (the third lot, printed as '118', presumably 188); d-methamphetamine 5 against 10 mg/mL (twofold, recomputed), MDMA 50 against 2.5-5, lidocaine 100 against 2.5, diphenhydramine 100 against 0.5-1 mg/mL. Editors' fold range recomputed: lidocaine 40, MDMA 10 and 20, diphenhydramine 100 and 200, so '10 to 200' is the correct arithmetic; the authors themselves write 10- to 100-fold (Conclusion, 2nd paragraph). Separate testing rounds (2017; summer 2022) and no storage or expiry information confirmed; the strips also reached the laboratory by donation from DanceSafe and San Francisco AIDS Foundation (Funding), although Methods says they were obtained from BTNX, so their storage history before testing is unknown. The two 2017 lots did not differ from each other; the three 2021 lots differed by one to two dilution steps for analogues (Conclusion, 1st paragraph).

anchors.locator: Methods › Standards, reagents, test strips, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: BTNX Rapid Response fentanyl strips, 20 ng/mL urine cut-off, five lots (D607082, 16120004, DOA2101018, DOA2111188, DOA2105196). Lots 082 and 004 obtained and evaluated in 2017; lots 018, 188, 196 obtained in 2021 and evaluated in summer 2022; same principal investigator and laboratory in both rounds. No storage conditions or expiry dates are given anywhere in the paper.

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 1
anchors.extracted: Fentanyl in water: 2017 lots positive down to 20 ng/mL (the stated cut-off); 2021 lots only down to 200 ng/mL, an order of magnitude above it. Duplicate strips, consensus reading.

anchors.locator: Results › Urine and water as test strip eluent comparison, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: In drug-free urine the three 2021 lots did better than in water: lowest positive 50 ng/mL for lots 018 and 196 and 100 ng/mL for the third (printed '118'); lines brighter in urine. Data in Fig. S2 (not opened).

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip interferences, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Fig. 2
anchors.extracted: 2017 lots: diphenhydramine and lidocaine positive at 100 mg/mL, MDMA at 50 mg/mL, d-methamphetamine at 5 mg/mL. 2021 lots: lidocaine 2.5 and d-methamphetamine 10 mg/mL on all three; MDMA 5 (018, 188) and 2.5 mg/mL (196); diphenhydramine 0.5 (018, 188) and 1 mg/mL (196).

anchors.locator: Fig. 2 (diphenhydramine, lidocaine, MDMA panels: 'Not tested' cells); Results › Fentanyl test strip interferences, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: 2017 lots were tested only at diphenhydramine 150, 100 (positive) and 50 mg/mL (negative), lidocaine 150-25, MDMA 50-25 and methamphetamine 10-2.5 mg/mL. The 2021 lots read diphenhydramine negative at 50 mg/mL (lot 196 invalid) and lots 188 and 196 also at 100 mg/mL, positive again at 25 down to 0.5-1 mg/mL: paradoxical high-concentration negatives, repeated, unexplained. Direct lot contrasts exist for lidocaine (25-50 mg/mL), MDMA (25 mg/mL) and d-methamphetamine (5 mg/mL), not for diphenhydramine.

anchors.locator: Conclusion, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: No lot-to-lot variability between the two 2017 lots; among 2021 lots analogue sensitivities often differed by one to two dilution steps. Authors summarize the interference change as a 10- to 100-fold increase in sensitivity for diphenhydramine, lidocaine and MDMA, and a decrease for d-methamphetamine (threshold 10 mg/mL).

anchors.locator: Funding, 1st paragraph (with Acknowledgements)
anchors.extracted: All strip lots except DOA2101018 were provided through DanceSafe (coordinated by a community advocate who had raised the lot-variability issue); lot DOA2101018 was donated by San Francisco AIDS Foundation. Lot 196 was the lot community advocates had reported as defective (Background, 7th paragraph). Handling before arrival not described.

claims.note: Halifax numbers in the claim match: 20 ng/mL (two 2017 lots) against 200 ng/mL (three 2021 lots), duplicate strips; 4 of 173 BC drug-checking samples missed (4/173 = 2.3%, as printed), all with fentanyl at 5% by weight or less, second-hand from McCrae et al. 2020 (Halifax says the samples were confirmed by laboratory qNMR and tested at about 30 µg/mL). Editors' '25-fold range' recomputed: 500/20 = 25, its lower end being this paper's 2017 lots. Halifax Table 1 relays earlier BTNX limits of 100 (Green), 50 (Bergh), 25 (Lockwood), 100 (Wharton) and 200 ng/mL (Park); the Bergh figure of 50 ng/mL differs from the claim's 'positive at 100 ng/mL' for Bergh and should be checked against Bergh itself (not read here).

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 1 (fentanyl panel)
anchors.extracted: Fentanyl spiked into water, two strips per lot and concentration, manufacturer's reading by two people, consensus: lowest positive 20 ng/mL for lots 082 and 004 (2017), 200 ng/mL for lots 018, 188 and 196 (2021); negative at 10 ng/mL and at 100 ng/mL respectively.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 4th paragraph
anchors.extracted: Second-hand (McCrae et al. 2020, ref. 57): in British Columbia drug-checking samples confirmed by laboratory qNMR, strips missed fentanyl in 4 of 173 fentanyl-positive samples (2.3%), all four with fentanyl at 5% by weight or less; samples tested at about 30 µg/mL; 70% expected opioids, 9% expected stimulants; fixed site with staff experienced in strip use, which the authors say limits generalizability.

anchors.locator: Background, 6th paragraph; Table 1
anchors.extracted: Previous independent BTNX 20 ng/mL evaluations gave fentanyl limits of detection of 100 (Green 2020), 50 (Bergh 2021), 25 (Lockwood 2021), 100 (Wharton 2021) and 200 ng/mL (Park 2022); only one approached the stated 20 ng/mL.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Authors: the 20 ng/mL cut-off is urine-specific and cannot be extrapolated to drug dissolved in water; urine cut-offs were also lot-dependent (best 50 ng/mL).

claims.overstatement: The claim lists '100 ... mg/mL for diphenhydramine' as the 2017 lots' threshold beside 0.5-1 mg/mL for the 2021 lots, but the 2017 lots were tested only at 150, 100 and 50 mg/mL, and the 2021 lots themselves read negative at 50 mg/mL (188 and 196 also at 100 mg/mL) while positive from 25 down to 0.5-1 mg/mL, so the 2017 figure is not a comparable threshold. The claim also omits these paradoxical negatives, which qualify 'strong solutions ... turned the strip positive' and 'false positives (0.5 mg/mL and above)' for diphenhydramine on the 2021 lots.
claims.note: All other Halifax numbers match: d-methamphetamine 5 and 10, MDMA 50 and 2.5-5, lidocaine 100 and 2.5, diphenhydramine 0.5-1 mg/mL (2021 lots); l-methamphetamine negative at 25 mg/mL, cocaine and ketamine at 25 mg/mL (2017 lots), levamisole to 100 mg/mL (2021 lots); also heroin, 6-acetylcodeine and quinidine at 10 µg/mL negative (2017 lots). Pure standards; duplicates by reference to the sensitivity procedure. Fig. 2 and text disagree on one cell: the text says consensus negatives at 50 and 100 mg/mL diphenhydramine on the 2021 lots, but Fig. 2 shows lot 018 positive at 100 mg/mL. Editors' comparison '1,000 to 25,000 times' recomputed: 0.5 mg/mL / 500 ng/mL = 1,000 and / 20 ng/mL = 25,000, arithmetic correct, but it pairs the lowest false-positive concentration (Halifax 2021 lots) with detection limits from other lots and studies; within the same strips the ratio is 2,500 for the Halifax 2021 lots (0.5 mg/mL against 200 ng/mL) and 250,000 for the 2017 lots (5 mg/mL against 20 ng/mL). The authors' dilution reasoning (Additional file 3) is modelled, not tested on real samples.

anchors.locator: Methods › Interferences, 1st paragraph; Methods › Strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Pure analytical standards of drugs, adulterants and cutting agents diluted in water, top concentration up to 150 mg/mL where available (some limited to 10, 25 or 50 mg/mL by supply); same procedure as for sensitivity (duplicate strips, two readers, consensus, read within 5 min).

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip interferences, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: 2017 lots: heroin, 6-acetylcodeine, quinidine (10 µg/mL), cocaine and ketamine (25 mg/mL) no cross-reactivity; l-methamphetamine negative at 25 mg/mL; positives with diphenhydramine and lidocaine at 100 mg/mL, MDMA at 50 mg/mL, d-methamphetamine at 5 mg/mL.

anchors.locator: Results › Fentanyl test strip interferences, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: 2021 lots: lidocaine 2.5 and d-methamphetamine 10 mg/mL on all three; MDMA 5 (018, 188) and 2.5 mg/mL (196); levamisole no cross-reactivity up to 100 mg/mL; diphenhydramine positive at 0.5 (018, 188) and 1 mg/mL (196) but consensus negative at 50 and 100 mg/mL with faint control lines and very faint to invisible test lines, repeated with the same result; lot 196 gave no control line at 50 mg/mL (invalid).

anchors.locator: Fig. 2 (diphenhydramine panel)
anchors.extracted: Diphenhydramine: 2017 lots tested only at 150 and 100 (positive) and 50 mg/mL (negative). 2021 lots: all positive at 150; lot 018 positive at 100 (the text says negative), 188 and 196 negative at 100; all negative or invalid at 50; positive from 25 down to 0.5 (018, 188) or 1 mg/mL (196); negative at 0.25 and below.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 2nd, 3rd and 6th paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Authors call 2.5-5 (MDMA), 2.5 (lidocaine) and 0.5-1 mg/mL (diphenhydramine) realistic testing concentrations; dilution advice built on 2017 lots would leave 2021-lot strips open to diphenhydramine or MDMA false positives; only 11 drugs and adulterants were evaluated, so other substances could also give false positives.

key_findings.note: Matches the Methods list; Fig. 1 itself has a tenth row at 50 000 ng/mL that the Methods do not list (see finding 3).

Fig. 1 fentanyl panel: 2017 lots positive 50 000 to 20 ng/mL, negative at 10; 2021 lots positive down to 200, negative at 100 and below. Editors' 0.001% and 0.01% recomputed (20 and 200 ng/mL in 2 mg/mL).

key_findings.correction: '(highest 10 µg/mL)' follows the Methods, but Fig. 1 has rows up to 50 000 ng/mL, and alfentanil and U-47700 are negative in every cell including 50 000 ng/mL. The 2017 lots detected sufentanil only at 10 000 and 50 000 ng/mL.

Per-lot lowest positive concentrations from Fig. 1 (ng/mL; lots 004/082/018/188/196): 3-methylfentanyl 500/500/1000/1000/500; acetyl fentanyl 500/500/100/100/50; acrylfentanyl 100/100/500/500/100; beta-OH-thiofentanyl 1000/1000/100/100/100; butyrylfentanyl 100/100/200/500/200; carfentanil 500/500/1000/10 000/10 000; cyclopropylfentanyl 100/100/200/500/100; fluorobutyrylfentanyl 5000 on all; furanyl fentanyl 5000/5000/500/500/200; p-fluorofentanyl 5000/5000/200/200/100; THF fentanyl 100 on all; sufentanil 10 000/10 000/none/none/none. The 2021 gain is therefore 5- to 10-fold for acetyl fentanyl (5-fold on lots 018 and 188), 10-fold for beta-OH-thiofentanyl, 10- to 25-fold for furanyl fentanyl and 25- to 50-fold for p-fluorofentanyl, so the authors' 'ten to fifty times' is slightly generous. Two series are non-monotone: carfentanil lot 018 positive at 50 000, 10 000 and 1000 but negative at 5000 and 500; acrylfentanyl lot 196 positive at 100 but negative at 200 ng/mL.

key_findings.note: 200-fold recomputed (2 mg/mL over 10 µg/mL). These substances are text-only; Fig. 2 shows only diphenhydramine, lidocaine, MDMA and methamphetamine.

Fig. 2 agrees for lidocaine (2021 lots positive 150 to 2.5, negative at 1 and 0.5), MDMA (018 and 188 positive to 5, negative at 2.5; 196 positive to 2.5, negative at 1) and methamphetamine (positive 150 to 10, negative at 5 and below).

key_findings.correction: Fig. 2 differs from the text in one cell: at 100 mg/mL lot 018 is positive and only lots 188 and 196 are negative; at 50 mg/mL lots 018 and 188 are negative and lot 196 invalid; at 150 mg/mL all three 2021 lots are positive again. So the paradoxical negatives are at 50 mg/mL (all) and 100 mg/mL (two of three lots).

Arithmetic recomputed and correct, but the diphenhydramine figure is not a demonstrated change: Fig. 2 shows the 2017 lots were tested with diphenhydramine only at 150, 100 (positive) and 50 mg/mL (negative; everything below 'Not tested'), and the 2021 lots also read negative at 50 mg/mL while positive from 25 down to 0.5-1 mg/mL, so a 2017 negative at 50 mg/mL does not show the 2017 lots would stay negative at 0.5-25 mg/mL. Direct contrasts exist for lidocaine (2017 negative at 25 and 50 mg/mL, 2021 positive), MDMA (2017 negative at 25 mg/mL, 2021 positive) and d-methamphetamine (2017 positive at 5 mg/mL, 2021 negative). Cite 10- to 40-fold (MDMA, lidocaine) and twofold (d-methamphetamine) as shown; for diphenhydramine give only the 2021 thresholds.

key_findings.note: All Table 1 values checked on the table page.
Fig. 1 panels confirm remifentanil, ocfentanil and valeryl fentanyl absent; norfentanyl, also named in the maker's claim, was not tested either.

reporting_issues.note: Beyond the summary range, the diphenhydramine part of the change is not established by the design (see key finding 8).
These three are text-only (not in Fig. 2), so whether 10 µg/mL is a misprint cannot be checked.

Within the 2021 round, analogue and interference limits did differ by one or two steps (Figs. 1-2), so the abstract's variability statement holds for analogues and interferents, not for fentanyl within a round.
Fig. 1 shows one consensus cell per lot and concentration; the two non-monotone series (carfentanil lot 018, acrylfentanyl lot 196) are visible signs of that unmeasured variation.

risk_of_bias.note: Sample selection high (two-gate, pure single analytes), index test unclear (consensus only, faint-line rule and reader blinding not reported; readers presumably knew each vial's content), reference standard low, overall high: agree. Flow and timing high is defensible because the lot comparison, which is what the claims use, is confounded with testing round and unequal panels (Fig. 2 shows the 2017 lots were tested over narrower concentration ranges: diphenhydramine only 150-50 mg/mL, MDMA only 50-25 mg/mL); for the accuracy of each lot within its own round this domain would be low.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor agreed, with two additions from Fig. 2. (1) The card's open question is answered: Fig. 2 has no 2 mg/mL step for MDMA (rows 150, 100, 50, 25, 10, 5, 2.5, 1, 0.5); at 2.5 mg/mL only lot 196 was positive and at 1 mg/mL none, so the authors' warning that 2 mg/mL dilution leaves 2021-lot strips open to MDMA false positives (Discussion, 3rd paragraph) is an extrapolation for MDMA, while it holds for diphenhydramine. (2) The Conclusion's 10- to 100-fold increase in sensitivity to diphenhydramine is not shown, because the 2017 lots were never tested in the range where the 2021 lots reacted.

missed: Fig. 1 has ten concentration rows, up to 50 000 ng/mL, against the nine (to 10 µg/mL) in the Methods; the card's 'nine concentrations from 10 µg/mL to 10 ng/mL' (design_detail, sample) follows the Methods. Sufentanil (2017 lots) and carfentanil (lots 188 and 196) were detected only at 10 000 ng/mL and above.

Fig. 2 'Not tested' cells: the 2017 lots were tested over narrow ranges only (diphenhydramine 150-50, lidocaine 150-25, MDMA 50-25, methamphetamine 10-2.5 mg/mL), which the card's comparison field lists as unknown; this limits every 2017-against-2021 threshold comparison and removes the diphenhydramine one.
Text and Fig. 2 disagree on diphenhydramine at 100 mg/mL for lot 018 (text negative, figure positive); a further reporting issue.

Non-monotone results in Fig. 1 (carfentanil lot 018; acrylfentanyl lot 196) show that a single consensus reading per step can flip between adjacent concentrations, relevant to the card's power and index-test notes.
